A wrong-message set necessarily has positive total rate, since the zero-rate message sets are singletons. If both rates are zero, the unique message pair is always returned with zero error. Scaling any nonnegative pair in the displayed closed region by $1-\varepsilon$, with $0<\varepsilon<1$, makes every positive-total-rate subset inequality strict; letting $\varepsilon$ decrease to zero therefore gives all closed faces, including cases where a zero-rate subset has zero information.
